newsitem.title: USA: Merck gets FDA ok to market Comvax.
newsitem.headline: Merck gets FDA ok to market Comvax.

text.p: Merck & Co Inc said Friday the U.S. Food and Drug Adminstration has licensed it to market Comvax as a vaccination for infants against both Haemophilus influenzae type b diseases and hepatitis B.
Comvax is the first combination product for vaccinating infants as young as two months for Haemophilus influenzae type B and hepatitis B.

Comvax combines two vaccines currently marketed by Merck, liquid PedvaxHIB, a haemophilus b conjugate vaccine and Recombivax HBO, a hepatitis B vaccine. Comvax should be available in January, the company said.

Comvax would be given with other pediatric vaccines as an intramuscular injection, Merck said. The company said it has been shown to be "generally well tolerated and highly immunogenic" in infants of six weeks to 15 months old.
